title: A Frosty Morning
note: A thin white frost covers every leaf, twig and blade of grass.
light: Keep the shadows pale blue and leave the paper bare for the frost.
shadow: for the blue shadows, pressed lightly
highlight: for the frost along the edges of things

title: Evening Sun
phrases: warm orange light on one side
note: The sun is low in the sky and lights one side of everything a warm orange.
light: Colour the sunny side of each thing a warm orange and pull its shadow out long behind it.
highlight: for the sunny side of each thing

title: A Rainy Afternoon
note: Steady rain falls from an even grey sky and everything looks wet.
light: Keep all the colours soft and greyish, and leave small spots of white paper for the wet shine.
highlight: for the shine on wet things

title: Dusk
note: The sun has just set and everything under the sky turns a deep, cool blue.
light: Colour everything in cool blues first, then add any lamp or lit window as a warm yellow spot.
highlight: for the last light in the sky

title: By Lamplight
note: A single lamp makes a pool of yellow light and everything outside it goes dim.
light: Choose where the lamp is, keep the brightest colours right beside it and get darker as you move away.
shadow: for the dim edges away from the lamp
highlight: for the surfaces facing the lamp

title: A Bright, Snowy Morning
note: Fresh snow lies smooth over everything and the sky is clear blue.
light: Leave the snow as bare white paper and shade only the dips, very lightly, in a cool blue or grey.
shadow: for the shadows in the snow
highlight: for the snow in the sun

title: A Stormy Afternoon
note: Dark clouds pile up overhead and the light underneath turns an odd yellow.
light: Make the background a dark purple-grey and keep the light on the main subject bright and yellowish.
highlight: for the brightest light under the clouds

title: A Warm Summer Night
phrases: a deep blue sky, not black
note: The sky never goes fully black, and a pale glow stays low along one edge.
light: Use a deep blue instead of black for the darkest parts.
shadow: for the deep blue that takes the place of black
highlight: for the pale glow low in the sky

title: A Misty Morning
note: A soft white mist hangs in the air and anything far away fades to pale grey.
light: Keep every edge soft and every colour pale, with no hard darks anywhere.
highlight: for the misty light

title: A Windy Autumn Day
note: Strong wind blows leaves through the air and clouds race across the sky.
light: Make your pencil strokes quick and slanted one way, so the whole picture leans with the wind.
shadow: for the shade under passing clouds
highlight: for the bursts of sunshine

title: A Sunny Spring Day
note: The light is clear and bright, and new leaves are just opening.
light: Keep the colours light and clear, with yellowy greens and plenty of white paper showing.
highlight: for the sunlit tops of things

title: Just After the Rain
note: Everything is dripping and shining, and the sun is already back out.
light: Use rich, strong colours and leave a tiny dot of white paper on every drop and wet edge.
highlight: for the sparkle on every drop

title: Under a Full Moon
note: The moon is bright enough to cast shadows, and every colour turns silver and blue.
light: Colour the darkest parts first and leave the moonlit tops of things almost bare.
highlight: for the moonlight on the tops of things

title: A Scorching Hot Day
note: The sun is high and white, the shadows are small and the air shimmers.
light: Keep the sunny parts very pale, almost white, and make the shadows small and very dark.
shadow: for the small dark shadows right under things
highlight: for the sun-bleached tops of things

title: A Drizzly Day
note: Fine drizzle hangs in the air and the light stays flat and grey all day.
light: Tone every colour down with a light layer of grey and avoid strong darks.
highlight: for the dull shine on damp surfaces

title: Sunrise
note: The sun is just coming up, and the sky turns from grey to peach and pink.
light: Colour the side of each thing facing the sun a soft peach, and keep the rest a cool grey-blue.
highlight: for the first sunlight on the edges of things

title: A Cloudy Afternoon
note: Thin cloud covers the sun, so the light is soft and the shadows have no hard edges.
light: Blend the edges of every shadow so that none of them has a hard line.
highlight: for the gentle light from the cloudy sky

title: A Big Orange Moon
when: as a big orange moon rises
note: A huge orange moon sits just above the horizon in a darkening blue sky.
light: Make the moon the warmest, brightest thing in the picture and keep everything else darker.
highlight: for the moon and its glow

title: Fireworks
when: while fireworks light up the sky
phrases: bright sparks on a dark sky
note: Fireworks burst in bright colours, smoke drifts low and everything is lit from one side.
light: Leave the fireworks as bare paper first, then colour the dark sky around them.
highlight: for the sparks and their glow

title: A Dark Winter Afternoon
note: The sun is already sinking and the light fades early to grey and blue.
light: Keep most of the picture dark and cool, with just one strip of pale, cold light.
highlight: for the pale, cold light low in the sky

title: A Cold, Cloudy Evening
note: Low clouds with a pinkish-grey tinge cover the sky and nothing moves.
light: Use soft pinkish greys for everything, with no bright colour anywhere.
highlight: for the pale sky

title: A Sunny Morning
note: The sun is well up, the sky is blue and the light is clean and bright.
light: Keep it light and loose, with lots of white paper and only a few firm darks.
highlight: for the bright morning light

title: While the Kettle Boils
note: Steam curls up from the spout and mists the nearest window.
light: Soften a few edges with your lightest pencil, as if steam has drifted across.
highlight: for the steam and the misted window

title: By Firelight
note: The fire throws a flickering orange light and shadows move on the walls.
light: Make the side facing the fire bright orange, and let the far side drop into a deep, warm brown.
shadow: for the deep darks away from the fire
highlight: for the glow on the side nearest the flames

title: A Dewy Morning
phrases: drops of dew on the grass
note: Tiny drops of water cover the grass and leaves and catch the early sun.
light: Leave a tiny dot of bare paper on every drop of dew, with a small dark edge beside it.
shadow: for the shadows and the dark side of each drop
highlight: for the early sun on the wet grass

title: A Foggy Day
note: Thick fog sits over everything, and anything more than a few steps away disappears.
light: Draw the nearest thing clearly, then make everything behind it greyer and fainter until it disappears into the paper.
shadow: for the few darks close to you
highlight: for the fog in the distance

title: Blossom Time
phrases: pink and white flowers on the trees
note: The trees are covered in pink and white flowers, and petals drift down in the breeze.
light: Keep the pinks clean and pale, and use a cool green for the shadows so the blossom stays fresh.
shadow: for the shady parts under the blossom
highlight: for the palest petals

title: Sunset
note: The sun sits on the horizon and the sky glows pink and orange.
light: Colour the lit side of each thing a warm pink-orange, and add a little purple to the shadows.
highlight: for the sunset light on the edges of things

title: A Cold, Clear Morning
note: The sky is a clear, deep blue and every edge looks sharp.
light: Use a sharp pencil point and firm edges, and keep the shadows crisp and clean.
highlight: for the bright, cold sunshine

title: A Hazy Autumn Afternoon
note: The sun is soft and hazy, and the light has a gentle yellow warmth.
light: Lay a pale yellow layer over everything first, then build the reds and browns on top.
highlight: for the sun on rounded surfaces

title: Sunshine and Showers
when: on a day of sunshine and showers
note: Quick showers sweep through while the sun keeps breaking out between them.
light: Draw the rain as a few light, slanting strokes of pale blue and keep the sunlit parts bright.
shadow: for the dark grey rain clouds
highlight: for the sunlight between the showers

title: Daffodil Time
note: Clumps of yellow daffodils are out everywhere and the light is clear and fresh.
light: Use clean, bright yellows for anything in the sun and keep the shadows a cool, pale green.
shadow: for the shadows under the leaves
highlight: for the brightest sunlit petals

title: Just Before Sunrise
phrases: a faint glow along one edge
note: The sky is just starting to lighten along one edge, but the ground is still dark.
light: Work in dark blues and greys, and lighten only a thin strip of sky along one edge.
shadow: for the dark ground and shapes
highlight: for the first faint light in the sky

title: Under the Stars
when: under a sky full of stars
note: There is no moon, the sky is full of stars and everything below is a dark shape.
light: Press the stars into the paper first with an empty ballpoint pen, then colour the dark sky over them so they stay white.
shadow: for the night sky and the dark shapes
highlight: for the stars

title: A Warm Summer Afternoon
note: The sun is warm, the air is still and the shade gathers in soft pools.
light: Keep the sunlit parts warm and light, and let the shade gather in soft, darker pools.
highlight: for the warm afternoon sunlight

title: Low Winter Sun
note: The sun stays low all day and throws long, slanting light under everything.
light: Leave the sunlit edges almost white and stretch the shadows right across the page.
highlight: for the dazzle where the sun hits

title: Autumn Colours
note: The trees are turning orange, red and yellow, and the low sun makes the colours glow.
light: Layer yellow first, then orange, then a touch of red, so the autumn colours glow.
highlight: for the sunlit edges of the leaves

title: Falling Snow
note: Big, slow flakes keep falling and everything is turning white.
light: Keep everything pale, and leave small dots of bare paper for the falling flakes.
shadow: for the few dark things the snow hasn't covered
highlight: for the snow on the tops of things

title: By Candlelight
note: One candle flame lights a small circle and the rest of the room fades into dark.
light: Leave one bright spot of paper for the flame, let the light fade quickly around it and keep everything else very dark.
shadow: for the deep dark beyond the candle
highlight: for the circle of candlelight

title: A Wet Autumn Day
note: Wet leaves lie stuck flat to the ground and everything looks damp and brown.
light: Use muddy browns and dull oranges, then add a few sharp white highlights so the wet leaves shine.
highlight: for the shine on wet leaves
